title: Seventh Word Satans Deception And The Dialogue Over Talisman Medicine And Ticket

questions.question: What did the tricky man bring with him when he came to the soldier?
questions.answer: He brought fancy things, exciting images, and drinks that could cloud the mind.

questions.question: What kind of life was the man inviting the soldier to enjoy?
questions.answer: He was calling him to fun, pleasure, and careless enjoyment.

questions.question: What was the soldier quietly saying to himself?
questions.answer: He was repeating a protective prayer-like formula.

questions.question: How did the tricky man speak about the soldier’s recitation?
questions.answer: He treated it like useless words and told him to stop.

questions.question: What did the soldier say he was holding in his hand?
questions.answer: He said it was a healing remedy.

questions.question: Why did the tricky man tell the soldier to throw the medicine away?
questions.answer: He wanted the soldier to think he was fine and should just enjoy himself.

questions.question: How did the man try to make the soldier give up the paper?
questions.answer: He told him to tear it up and forget about the journey.

questions.question: What does the passage show about the soldier’s response to this man?
questions.answer: The soldier started to be influenced by him for a while.

questions.question: What lesson about people is stated after this?
questions.answer: People can be fooled by clever tricks.

questions.question: From which side did the warning voice come?
questions.answer: It came from the right.

questions.question: What was the first message of the strong voice?
questions.answer: It warned the soldier not to be tricked.

questions.question: What four dangers did the voice say the man would have to remove before he could be trusted?
questions.answer: He would have to defeat the lion, take away the gallows, stop the wounds, and cancel the journey ahead.

questions.question: Whom was the soldier told to speak like?
questions.answer: He was told to speak like the Allah-inspired guide who had helped him before.

questions.question: How is the man who came from the left described?
questions.answer: He is shown as sneaky, immoral, and very deceptive.

questions.question: Why did he show the soldier decorated things and pleasant entertainment?
questions.answer: He wanted to tempt the soldier and pull him away from what would truly help him.

questions.question: What did the soldier call the words he was repeating?
questions.answer: He called them a talisman, meaning a protection and help for him.

questions.question: What does the tricky man’s reaction to the talisman tell us about him?
questions.answer: It shows he did not value spiritual help and wanted the soldier to forget it.

questions.question: What two objects besides the talisman did the soldier have?
questions.answer: He had a medicine and a paper for travel and provisions.

questions.question: How did the tricky man describe the soldier’s condition?
questions.answer: He claimed the soldier was healthy and should just celebrate.

questions.question: What season did the man mention, and why?
questions.answer: He mentioned spring to make the moment seem too pleasant to think seriously about the future.

questions.question: What do the man’s words suggest about his attitude toward the journey?
questions.answer: He wanted the soldier to ignore it as if it did not matter.

questions.question: What happened to the soldier after hearing all this persuasion?
questions.answer: He was partly convinced and began to lean toward the trickster’s words.

questions.question: What personal confession is made in the passage?
questions.answer: The speaker admits being misled by similar deception.

questions.question: What was special about the voice that came from the right?
questions.answer: It was powerful and commanding, like thunder.

questions.question: What challenge was the trickster given?
questions.answer: He was told to prove he could remove the soldier’s real dangers.

questions.question: What should the soldier do if the trickster cannot solve those dangers?
questions.answer: He should tell him to be quiet.

questions.question: Who approached the soldier after some time?
questions.answer: A deceitful man came to him from the left.

questions.question: What kinds of things did this man use to attract the soldier?
questions.answer: He used luxury, exciting sights, music, food, and intoxicating drink.

questions.question: What did the soldier say when asked what he was murmuring?
questions.answer: He said it was a talisman.

questions.question: How did the man try to make the soldier think about the present moment?
questions.answer: He pushed him to chase immediate fun instead of thinking deeply.

questions.question: What did the soldier say about the object in his hand?
questions.answer: He said it was medicine.

questions.question: What were the two uses of the marked paper?
questions.answer: It was for travel and for getting provisions.

questions.question: How did the man talk about the future journey?
questions.answer: He acted as if there was no need to prepare for it.

questions.question: What warning does the sentence about human beings give us?
questions.answer: It teaches that people are able to be tricked if they are not careful.

questions.question: What happened suddenly to interrupt the deception?
questions.answer: A mighty warning voice came from the right.

questions.question: What was the very first command of that voice?
questions.answer: It told the soldier to stay alert and not be fooled.

questions.question: Name one threat behind the soldier and one threat in front of him that the voice mentioned.
questions.answer: Behind him was the lion, and in front of him was the gallows.

questions.question: Besides those two threats, what other troubles did the voice mention?
questions.answer: It mentioned the things hurting his two sides and the journey ahead.

questions.question: In this passage, what was the trickster trying to get the soldier to stop using?
questions.answer: He was trying to get him to give up the talisman, the medicine, and the travel paper.

questions.question: What does that tell us about the trickster’s goal?
questions.answer: His goal was to separate the soldier from the things that could protect and help him.

questions.question: What pleasures did the trickster offer first?
questions.answer: He offered drinking, entertainment, attractive pictures, music, and tasty food.

questions.question: How did he describe the soldier’s recited words?
questions.answer: He spoke of them as meaningless and bothersome.

questions.question: What did the trickster say about the soldier’s health?
questions.answer: He insisted that nothing was wrong with him.

questions.question: What did the man want done to the paper with five marks?
questions.answer: He wanted it destroyed.

questions.question: What excuse did he use for that?
questions.answer: He said the lovely time they were in made preparing for a journey unnecessary.

questions.question: How successful was the trickster at first?
questions.answer: He managed to influence the soldier somewhat.

questions.question: What feeling or weakness in people does the passage point out here?
questions.answer: It points out that people can be tricked by clever lies.

questions.question: What kind of speech did the warning voice use against the trickster?
questions.answer: It used a firm test, telling him to prove his power over the soldier’s dangers.

questions.question: What model of speech was the soldier told to copy?
questions.answer: He was told to answer in the way of the Allah-inspired guide.

questions.question: Where did the tempting man come from?
questions.answer: He came from the left.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest by describing him as devil-like in his cleverness?
questions.answer: It suggests that his tricks were harmful, sneaky, and spiritually dangerous.

questions.question: What three kinds of attraction did he use to pull the soldier in?
questions.answer: He used physical pleasure, beautiful-looking things, and mind-clouding drink.

questions.question: What was the first thing he questioned the soldier about?
questions.answer: He asked about the words the soldier was quietly repeating.

questions.question: How did the soldier identify those words?
questions.answer: He said they were a talisman.

questions.question: What was the second thing the man questioned?
questions.answer: He asked about the medicine in the soldier’s hand.

questions.question: What was the third thing the man questioned?
questions.answer: He asked about the marked paper the soldier was carrying.

questions.question: What pattern do you see in the man’s three questions?
questions.answer: He kept attacking each helpful thing the soldier had.

questions.question: Why did the man keep talking about fun and celebration?
questions.answer: He wanted the soldier to forget danger, duty, and preparation.

questions.question: What does the soldier’s partial persuasion teach about temptation?
questions.answer: Even someone who has help can still struggle and must stay careful.

questions.question: What proof from real life is added by the speaker after that?
questions.answer: The speaker says he too was fooled by similar tricks.

questions.question: What did the voice from the right tell the soldier to ask the trickster to do?
questions.answer: It told him to ask for proof that he could remove all the real threats around him.

questions.question: Why mention the lion, the gallows, the wounds, and the journey together?
questions.answer: They show that the soldier’s problems are deep and cannot be fixed by entertainment.

questions.question: What should happen if the trickster cannot meet the challenge?
questions.answer: He should stop talking and stop misleading the soldier.

questions.question: What was the mood of the man who approached the soldier?
questions.answer: He came with a playful and tempting mood meant to lure the soldier.

questions.question: How did he try to make his invitation sound attractive?
questions.answer: He spoke about partying, looking at pretty images, listening to music, and enjoying food.

questions.question: What did the soldier have that showed he was not just living for fun?
questions.answer: He had spiritual protection, healing help, and something to prepare for the road ahead.

questions.question: How did the trickster respond to each of those helpful things?
questions.answer: He told the soldier to stop using them or destroy them.

questions.question: What wrong message did the trickster give about the soldier’s condition?
questions.answer: He told him he had no real problem and should only enjoy the moment.

questions.question: Why is that message unwise based on the rest of the passage?
questions.answer: Because the soldier still faced serious dangers that pleasure could not remove.

questions.question: What does the line about human beings being deceived add to the story?
questions.answer: It makes the lesson broader by showing this struggle happens to people in general.

questions.question: What interrupted the soldier’s growing persuasion?
questions.answer: A powerful warning voice suddenly called out from the right.

questions.question: What was the soldier told to say before accepting the trickster’s offer?
questions.answer: He was told to demand that the man first remove every major danger facing him.

questions.question: What does this teach about listening to invitations from others?
questions.answer: We should test whether they lead to real good or just distract us.

questions.question: Why can’t pleasure alone solve the soldier’s problem?
questions.answer: Because enjoyment does not defeat danger, heal wounds, or prepare for the journey.

questions.question: How should the soldier answer the trickster if he fails the test?
questions.answer: He should reject his offer and tell him to keep quiet.
